exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS protocol versions enable downgrade attacks where an attacker forces the use of older, weaker protocol versions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Using weak TLS protocol versions directly weakens the encryption protecting communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can exploit missing or invalid TLS certificates to gather reconnaissance or conduct man-in-the-middle attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers may forge or obtain fraudulent certificates to impersonate servers with missing or invalid certificates.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext HTTP traffic can be intercepted via network sniffing, exposing all transmitted data to attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: System Information Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Server version disclosure allows attackers to gather system information to identify vulnerabilities in specific software versions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Software
exploitedBy.relevance: Disclosed server version information enables adversaries to gather victim host software details for targeted exploitation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File and Directory Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Enabled directory listing allows attackers to enumerate files and directories on the web server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Browser Session Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing security headers (e.g., missing HttpOnly or secure flags) can enable browser session hijacking attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: HTML Smuggling
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of security headers like Content-Security-Policy facilitates HTML smuggling and cross-site scripting attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Web Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted HTTP methods allow attackers to leverage web protocols for unauthorized actions such as PUT or DELETE operations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
exploitedBy.relevance: Processes running with excessive privileges can be exploited for privilege escalation to gain higher-level access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Create or Modify System Process
exploitedBy.relevance: Privileged process execution may involve creating or modifying system processes to maintain elevated access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured web root permissions directly relate to improper file and directory permission settings that can be exploited.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Services File Permissions Weakness
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak permissions on web root files can be exploited similarly to services file permission weaknesses for unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient access logging mirrors the impact of disabled or modified logs, leaving attacker activity undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient logging effectively blocks security indicators from being captured, aiding attacker evasion.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Log injection via uncontrolled format strings can be used to tamper with or corrupt log entries, similar to clearing logs.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can inject obfuscated or misleading entries into logs to hide malicious activity through uncontrolled log formats.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched server software exposes known vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit in public-facing applications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploits
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers obtain or use existing exploits specifically targeting unpatched server software vulnerabilities.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, servers are vulnerable to application exhaustion flood attacks that overwhelm application resources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reflection Amplification
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent request throttling enables reflection amplification attacks by allowing unlimited requests to be processed.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Default Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Default or sample content often includes default credentials that attackers can exploit to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Escape to Host
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured virtual host isolation can allow attackers to escape from one virtual host context to access other hosts or the underlying system.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Domain Fronting
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured virtual host isolation can be abused similarly to domain fronting to access unintended hosts or bypass controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed private key files directly enable attackers to steal private keys for decryption or impersonation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Private key file exposure represents a form of unsecured credentials that attackers can harvest for further attacks.
